proposals.evidence: DEDR4641 documents Tamil mañcu and Kota manj cloud, and Malayalam maññu/Kannada mañju mist or fog. These survey mañj-/mañc- cloud responses extend that documented family comparatively to minority lects. Palatal/affricate spellings and final vowels are preserved; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review, and no literal DEDR attestation is claimed for absent lects. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4682 gives Kannada and Kodagu maṇḍe, Kota maṇḍ and Toda maḍ ‘head’. Badaga manḍē is a comparative extension to the same head family, not a claim that this Badaga attestation is printed in the dictionary or that contact has been independently excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2460 gives Kannada sāre ‘nearness’ and explicitly describes Toda sōry ‘near’ as borrowed from Badaga. The source therefore independently supports a Badaga proximity word in this family; survey sāre/sārə preserves its own vowel notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3296 gives Kannada tuṭi/toḍi, Tulu duḍi and Kota tuc lip. The survey dental/retroflex and voicing variants are preserved; Badaga/Sholaga and Alu Kurumba are comparative lect extensions, and Kota tus is compared with the specifically attested Kota tuc. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
